help: Advanced Diplomacy adds new diplomatic trading options, from embassies to trading military and worker units.
name: Advanced Diplomacy

help: Allows for powerful espionage attacks, including nuclear sabatoge, aiding rebel factions, and causing empire-wide anarchy. Also, espionage effects, like poisoning water, will correctly scale for gamespeeds.
name: Advanced Espionage

help: Enables more advanced variations of Nuclear Weapons for your arsenal.
name: Advanced Nukes

help: Allows players to 'purchase' their choice of starting cities, units, technologies, etc. when game begins.
name: Advanced Start

help: AI leaders favor war over diplomacy
name: Aggressive AI

help: Civilizations cannot declare war on each other
name: Always Peace

help: All AI civilizations are at war with the human for the length of the game
name: Always War

help: Captured cities retain their original civilization, so they can build that Civ's UU's and Unique Buildings.
name: Assimilation

help: Enables XP and Great Generals from Barbarian Combat, but be warned, the Barbarians can receive Great Generals now too!
name: Barbarian Generals

help: The barbarians start with a free city for every civilization in the game
name: Barbarian World

help: Barbarians can not keep captured cities, and will always raze them.
name: Barbarians Always Raze

help: Unlocks a series of buildings, such as the moat, siege towers, and heavy gate, dedicated to expanding castles with key defense structures in your empire.
name: Expanded Castles

help: Every 50 turns (on Normal Speed) the player with the lowest score is removed from the game until only 5 players remain. Not meant for use with BarbarianCiv or Revolutions!
name: Final Five

help: Become the player with the highest score, then you switch to controlling the civilization with the lowest score. Raise that civilization to have the highest score and you will be switched again to civilization with the lowest score. That third civilization will be the one you have to win the game with. Single player only.
name: High to Low

help: Every 50 turns (on Normal Speed) the games difficulty is increased by 1 until it reaches Deity.
name: Increasing Difficulty

help: Allows the construction of a unique building that is unlocked for nearly every civic.
name: Civic Buildings

help: Must kill all cities Source units to wipe out an enemy civilization.
name: Require Complete Kills

help: Reassigns all starting locations according to the distances between civilizations on earth.
name: Culturally Linked Starts

help: Allows the construction of buildings designed for the very early game, as slower gamespeed games usually run out of things to build. Early buildings adds plenty of new early options, allow you to create infrastructure for city development.
name: Early Buildings

help: Cities which have been captured via conquest can convert peacefully back to a previous owner
name: City Flipping after Conquest

help: Great Commanders give Great Generals many bonuses for leading troops into battle, instead of just attaching to a squad of existing troops.
name: Great Commanders

help: Guilds adds new Medieval Guilds, which compete with one another and provide access to different unique benefits.
name: Guilds

help: Cities will be able to expand from a size two radius to a size three radius after acheiving the cultural distinction of "Influential"
name: Larger Cities

help: Players may lead any Civilization with any Leader.
name: Unrestricted Leaders

help: Civilizations can not found a new religion when controlling a Holy City.
name: Limited Religions

help: Sets a random admin password so that debug tools cannot be used, and the game assets cannot be modified. Only for single-player games.
name: Lock Modified Assets

help: 8 tiles around any city can never be conquered via cultural influence
name: Minimum City Border

help: Moderns Corporations adds new corporations for the modern era, making resources more valuble.
name: Modern Corporations

help: The Mountains Mod makes it so that mountains are no longer impassable, can have some resources, and can be worked by a city, like all other tiles.
name: Usable Mountains

help: Units cannot explore the map freely until certain techs are discovered
name: Movement Limits

help: When a city production is enough to finish more than one item, it can produce multiple items per turn.
name: Multiple Production

help: When a player has enough beakers to research more than one technology, and more than one technology is queued, they can research multiple technologies per turn.
name: Multiple Research

help: A new random seed is generated every time the game is reloaded - which, for example, will lead to different combat results
name: New Random Seed on Reload

help: Disables the BarbarianCivs: Barbarian cities which are left alone will remain barbarian, they will not spawn new civilizations.
name: No BarbarianCivs

help: No Barbarians or Animals will appear
name: No Barbarians

help: All civilizations are locked into either war or peace for the length of the game
name: Permanent War or Peace

help: Cities cannot convert peacefully from culture
name: No City Flipping From Culture

help: Cities cannot be razed after capture
name: No City Razing

help: Spies are not available, and Espionage Points are converted into Culture
name: No Espionage

help: Random Events do not occur
name: No Random Events

help: No fixed border mechanics, whether from civics or any other source
name: No Fixed Borders

help: Future and Transhuman Eras are disabled. The game ends at the end of the Modern Era.
name: No Transhuman Era

help: Random map generator does not place any tribal villages ("goody huts") on the map
name: No Tribal Villages

help: Disables Inquisitions.  Inquisitors may not be trained and non-state religions may not be purged in order to reduce the threat of rebellion.
name: No Inquisitions

help: Disables ALL Nuclear Weaponry.
name: No Nukes

help: Disables the Revolution mod component: new rebel civs will not attempt to breakaway from an empire if their needs are not being met.
name: No Revolutions

help: Players cannot trade technologies that they have not researched themselves
name: No Technology Brokering

help: Disables TechDiffusion: tech knowledge will not slowly diffuses to civs that are behind.
name: No TechDiffusion

help: Technologies cannot be traded via diplomacy
name: No Technology Trading

help: Disable Vassal State Treaties, which ensure a weaker civilization protection against a stronger rival
name: No Vassal States

help: The human player can never control more than one city
name: One-City Challenge

help: Two civilizations can form a Permanent Alliance which lasts the rest of the game
name: Permanent Alliances

help: Names key map locations, mountain ranges, deserts, forests, jungles, etc... on the game loadup.
name: Personalized Map

help: Players are prompted to pick a religion when they are about to found one.
name: Choose Religions

help: Increased Barbarian activity and aggressiveness
name: Raging Barbarians

help: Each AI leader's personality is determined randomly at game start
name: Random Personalities

help: Corporations will expand and grow dynamically, without player involvement, behaving more like real world Corporations, and not tied to central governments. Corporations can be taxed for a profit, or be subsidized by your nation to help it expand faster. It reduces the tedious micromanagement of corporations, and gives corporate policies real value and meaning.
name: Realistic Corporations

help: Culture spreads from Cities in a more realistic fashion, over low lying areas more quickly than peaks, hills, or jungles.
name: Realistic Culture Spread

help: Cities with many religions may have less popular ones slowly decay.
name: Religion Decay

help: Ruthless AI is a step up from Aggresive AI. The AI will be more backstabbing, less predictable, more ready to declare war on everyone, less likely to forgive past slights, and will trade with your worst enemies, just to spite you. Expect no mercy, for you shall receive none!
name: Ruthless AI

help: Surround and Destroy adds military bonuses for surrounding enemy troops and cities, simulating real world land ambushes
name: Surround and Destroy

help: All players start as minor civs, meaning they are at war with everyone.  Your civ will settle into a full civ and you'll be able to conduct diplomacy after you discover Writing.
name: Start as minor civs

help: The United Nations and Apostilitic Palace can still be built, even when diplomatic victory is not enabled. Players will be able to hold UN elections, but can not win by becoming the Secretary General.
name: United Nations

help: Removes the restriction on the number of wonders that can be built in one city
name: Unlimited Wonders
